security_spec.violation_condition: When KVM or the host kernel passes an 8B-aligned but non-page-aligned buf_addr to sbi_covh_promote_to_tvm(), the buffer [buf_addr, buf_addr + buf_size) may span two host physical pages. If the caller has only validated or pinned the starting page, the TSM writes secrets across a page boundary into memory the caller does not exclusively own.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: buf_addr & ~PAGE_MASK && !(crosses_page_boundary(buf_addr, buf_size) => get_user_pages for both pages)
security_spec.summary: Relaxing buf_addr alignment from 4 KiB to 8B means sbi_covh_promote_to_tvm() buffers can now straddle a page boundary; the kernel/KVM must pin both pages or risk TSM writing secrets into unrelated memory

location.file_path: N/A - code not present in this kernel tree

findings.finding: The function sbi_covh_promote_to_tvm() does not exist in the Linux 7.0-rc5 kernel tree. No SBI COVH/CoVE extension is defined, no attestation-related SBI code exists under arch/riscv/kvm/, and no RISC-V confidential computing guest driver exists under drivers/virt/coco/ (only x86 SEV-SNP and TDX guest drivers are present). The CoVE/realm support for RISC-V has not been upstreamed into this kernel version. The vulnerability condition described in the security spec cannot be triggered because the code under audit does not exist in this tree.
